conditions.text: The museum building is devised to Nicolas, or Olivia as simple substitute if Nicolas predeceases Rafael, refuses, or is incapable. Acquisition depends on the independent heritage board designating the building for preservation by 31 December 2025. It did so on 30 June 2025. Nicolas died in 2024; Olivia survived, accepted, and takes subject to the same property-related condition.
conditions.substitutionNote: Article 859 trigger: predecease. Article 862: the nonpersonal condition also binds Olivia. Nicolas's death does not transmit this testamentary gift through his estate.

conditions.text: Paolo and Rosa are each given PHP 2,000,000. Sofia alone replaces either or both if they predecease, repudiate, or cannot accept. Both executed valid repudiations after Rafael's death; Sofia accepted both legacies. There is no additional condition.
conditions.substitutionNote: One substitute for two instituted beneficiaries (Article 860). Do not invent three-axis coordinates for an unconditional substitution.

conditions.text: Tomas is devised the PHP 6,000,000 gallery. If he predeceases, repudiates, or cannot accept, Ursula and Victor replace him in expressly fixed shares of two-thirds and one-third. Tomas validly repudiated; both substitutes accepted. Whoever takes must promptly sign a conservation undertaking on learning of Rafael's death. Both signed immediately.
conditions.substitutionNote: Two substitutes for one beneficiary (Article 860); trigger is repudiation, not an assumed automatic substitution upon failure of a condition. Article 862 carries the undertaking to substitutes; Article 876 governs prompt compliance.

conditions.text: Waldo, Xenia, and Yasmin receive cash legacies of PHP 1,000,000, PHP 2,000,000, and PHP 3,000,000 and reciprocally substitute for one another on predecease, repudiation, or incapacity. Waldo repudiated; the others accepted. The will does not alter the statutory proportional rule.
conditions.substitutionNote: Article 861: distribute Waldo's PHP 1,000,000 between Xenia and Yasmin in their original ratio 2:3, not equally.

conditions.text: Leon receives the identified PHP 4,000,000 securities portfolio as fiduciary first heir, with an express obligation to preserve it and transmit it to his daughter Mira at his death. Leon and Mira were both alive and capable on 15 January 2025. No legitime is charged. At the 31 December 2025 accounting date Leon is alive and holds the portfolio.
conditions.substitutionNote: Articles 863–866: express preservation/transmission, one parent-child degree, both alive at opening, free portion only. Mira's right arises at Rafael's death, although delivery is deferred. This is a successive substitution, not a condition awaiting an uncertain event; no three-axis labels are forced on it.

conditions.text: Bruno receives an extra PHP 2,000,000, separate from his legitime, provided he does not cut the registered heritage tree on his own adjoining land during 2025. He furnished sufficient security under Article 879 and did not cut it. The accounting is after the period ended; no breach or return is due.
conditions.substitutionNote: Negative-condition security is essential: the geometric label does not mean the gift must simply remain undelivered until year end. Bruno's PHP 4,000,000 legitime is unconditional.

conditions.text: Clara receives an extra PHP 2,000,000 only if she submits the complete proposal and the independent city board approves the community reading-room project by 31 December 2025. She submitted it and the board approved it on 1 September 2025. After acquisition the gift ends if she personally diverts its capital to private use within three years; no diversion has occurred at the accounting date.
conditions.substitutionNote: Article 877: Clara's action and independent approval combine. A separate linked condition records the later resolutory clause so acquisition and loss are not conflated.

conditions.text: Clara's same PHP 2,000,000 reading-room gift, not a second gift, terminates if she diverts the capital to private use within three years after acquisition. She has not done so. The will directs any returned capital to Rafael's eight child-lines equally as an additional free-portion allocation, including Ana's descendants in equal subshares by express designation.
conditions.substitutionNote: Linked to the SAME reading-room disposition described under the mixed suspensive condition. This return clause does not burden any legitime. No contingent return is booked in the baseline.

story.narrative: Rafael Mercado built a museum and a commercial business through two successive marriages. His first wife Isabel died in 2000, survived by Rafael and their three legitimate children Ana, Bruno and Clara. Her estate and their marital property were fully settled before Rafael married Teresa in 2002 under a valid complete-separation marriage settlement. Rafael and Teresa had five legitimate children: Diego, Elena, Felipe, Gabriela and Hugo. Ana later died in 2023, leaving legitimate children Ines and Joaquin. Rafael died in 2025 leaving seven living children, Ana's represented line, and Teresa. His carefully itemized will protects all eight child-lines and the surviving wife, then places museum gifts, conditional legacies, and a father-to-daughter preservation portfolio in the free portion. Several voluntary beneficiaries predeceased or repudiated, activating different substitutions.
story.circumstances: Fictional Philippine-law exercise; valid marriages, legitimate filiation, capacity, probate and will formalities are stipulated. All first-marriage property claims were paid; only Rafael's adjudicated exclusive property is inventoried. Teresa's separate PHP16m is not an estate asset. No lifetime donations require collation. Post-death valuation changes, fruits, administrative costs beyond stated debts and taxes are assumed nil for the classroom arithmetic. Baseline distribution is as of31 December2025. All stated repudiations are valid and post-death; all actual takers accept.
keyFacts: Two successive wives, not two concurrent marriages. Isabel's death preceded the valid second marriage.
First marriage has three child-lines; second has five. Ana survived her mother and later predeceased her father, enabling representation.
Net estate64m; child legitimes32m; Teresa4m; disposable28m.
Substitution metadata is not an automatic condition classification. Unconditional clauses and the fideicommissary term deliberately remain unplotted.
The app currently permits one conditionId per disposition; Clara's second clause explicitly points to the same gift and is not a duplicate allocation.
The examples at the end of the guide are counterfactuals, not simultaneous changes to the64m baseline.

computationGuide.title: Fix the accounting snapshot
computationGuide.explanation: Rafael died 15 January 2025. This answer is the 31 December 2025 baseline: all stated conditions and repudiations above have occurred; Leon remains alive. Later return clauses and Mira's later delivery are not new assets.

computationGuide.title: Keep the first wife's estate separate
computationGuide.explanation: Isabel died in 2000 leaving Rafael and their three children. Her estate and the first marital property regime were fully liquidated, partitioned and paid before the second marriage. Ana survived that settlement. The figures below are Rafael's adjudicated property only; do not add Isabel's assets again.

computationGuide.title: Exclude Teresa's own property
computationGuide.explanation: The 2002 marriage used a valid complete-separation marriage settlement. Teresa owns 16,000,000 outside this inventory; Rafael owns the listed 68,000,000. No hypothetical half of Teresa's property is an inheritance. Her marital status and inheritance are separate questions.

computationGuide.title: Reconcile gross inventory
computationGuide.explanation: Museum 5m + gallery 6m + securities 4m + commercial complex 29m + cash 24m. Property values are Rafael's exclusive assets after the old settlement.

computationGuide.title: Deduct enforceable debts once
computationGuide.explanation: Museum mortgage 1m and commercial mortgage 2m are encumbrances; general bank debt 1m is separate. Testamentary gifts are not estate liabilities. No lifetime donations subject to collation, disputed ownership or additional estate charges are assumed.

computationGuide.title: Count eight equal child-lines
computationGuide.explanation: First marriage: Ana, Bruno, Clara. Second: Diego, Elena, Felipe, Gabriela, Hugo. Ana died in 2023 and her two legitimate children represent her. Count her ONE branch, not each grandchild as a ninth line. Seven children are personally alive; eight lines participate.

computationGuide.title: Reserve children's collective legitime
computationGuide.explanation: Under Article 888, reserve half of the 64m hereditary estate. Different marriages do not make one legitimate child's line smaller.

computationGuide.title: Divide by child-line
computationGuide.explanation: Each of eight lines receives 4m. In the first marriage block there is 12m collectively; in the second there is 20m. Do not first split 32m equally between marriages.

computationGuide.title: Apply representation
computationGuide.explanation: Ana receives nothing personally after predeceasing Rafael. Ines and Joaquin each receive half of her 4m branch. This is representation of Ana in Rafael's estate, not a transfer through Ana's estate.

computationGuide.title: Reserve surviving wife's legitime
computationGuide.explanation: Teresa alone is the surviving wife. Article 892 gives her an amount equal to one legitimate-child line, taken from the half otherwise disposable. Isabel receives zero in Rafael's 2025 estate.

computationGuide.title: Identify actual free portion
computationGuide.explanation: Children 32m + Teresa 4m = total protected 36m; the unburdened testamentary allocation pool is 28m, not 32m.

computationGuide.title: Simple substitution
computationGuide.explanation: The net museum devise is 5m less its 1m mortgage. Nicolas predeceased; Olivia was named to replace him and the heritage event occurred. Attribute the 4m net property to Olivia; not to Nicolas's heirs.

computationGuide.title: Compendious substitution
computationGuide.explanation: Paolo and Rosa each repudiated 2m. Their sole common substitute Sofia takes both. Sofia is not representing them.

computationGuide.title: Brief substitution
computationGuide.explanation: Tomas repudiated. Two named substitutes take the 6m gallery in the express ratio 2:1 after signing the undertaking. Ursula gets a 4m interest and Victor a 2m interest.

computationGuide.title: Reciprocal substitution
computationGuide.explanation: Only Waldo's 1m is vacant. Xenia and Yasmin were instituted in weights 2 and 3, so Xenia gets 1m ×2/5 =400,000 and Yasmin gets 600,000. Add each to her ORIGINAL legacy: Xenia 2.4m; Yasmin 3.6m. Do not redistribute the entire 6m pool.

computationGuide.title: Fideicommissary accounting
computationGuide.explanation: Leon holds the 4m portfolio subject to preserving and transmitting it to his living daughter Mira. Show 4m once among current holdings. Mira has a future-delivery right, not another present 4m deduction from the estate.

computationGuide.title: Resolve the additional conditions
computationGuide.explanation: Bruno receives 2m extra after furnishing security and observing the negative condition. Clara receives 2m extra after proposal plus approval; the resolutory diversion event has not occurred. Each also retains a 4m unconditional legitime.

computationGuide.title: Reconcile free-portion gifts
computationGuide.explanation: Olivia4 + Sofia4 + Ursula4 + Victor2 + Xenia2.4 + Yasmin3.6 + Leon4 + Bruno-extra2 + Clara-extra2 =28m. Every substitution stays within its original gift, not an extra allocation.

computationGuide.title: Final control total
computationGuide.explanation: Seven surviving child-lines 28m + two grandchildren 4m + Teresa4m =36m protected. Add28m gifts. Teresa's separate16m and Isabel's settled estate are excluded.

computationGuide.title: Counterfactual: term versus condition versus mode
computationGuide.explanation: Not part of the baseline totals: if Clara's gift were payable on a fixed future date, distinguish acquired rights from deferred enjoyment (Articles 878, 885). If it were simply charged with maintaining a reading room without an intent to suspend acquisition, examine mode and security (Article 882). Neither should be plotted as an invented suspensive condition.

computationGuide.title: Counterfactual: protect legitimes and detect reduction
computationGuide.explanation: Not an additional gift in this case: an extra unpreferred cash legacy of 7m would increase otherwise payable devises/legacies from28m to35m. Assuming all are reducible on the same footing and no priority, the pro-rata factor is28/35=0.8; do not reduce the36m legitimes. Actual indivisible real property can require Article912 treatment, so this variant assumes divisible value interests or agreed cash settlement.

computationGuide.title: Counterfactual: preterition, disinheritance and accretion
computationGuide.explanation: All compulsory lines are expressly covered here; no preterition or disinheritance occurs. Removing a direct-line heir entirely or asserting a legally insufficient disinheritance needs separate Article854/918 analysis, not simple subtraction. A valid named substitute prevents treating that same vacancy as automatic accretion. Representation of a repudiating heir is not permitted (Article977). These are alternative exercises, not cumulative baseline events.

explanation: Read the numbered guide for the baseline and clearly separated counterfactuals. This exercise integrates sequential marital-property settlement, legitimate descendants from different marriages, representation, all five named substitution structures, positive/negative and potestative/casual/mixed conditions, suspensive/resolutory effects, fiduciary versus absolute holdings, and reconciliation. Term, mode, reduction, preterition, disinheritance and accretion are contrast questions rather than contradictory events forced into the same distribution.

First-estate settlement and complete-separation property ownership are express givens, not inferred by the engine.

Terminology: brief means several substitutes for one; compendious means one substitute for several. The prior 15-case library is not revised or certified by this new example.
